concepts.title: 1. Product, Quotient & Power Rules
concepts.subtitle: Combining Exponents of the Same Base
concepts.summary: When multiplying powers with identical bases, add the exponents. When dividing powers with identical bases, subtract the exponents. When raising a power to another power, multiply the exponents.

points.text: Product Rule: $a^m \times a^n = a^{m+n}$. The bases MUST be identical.

concepts.trap: Do not add or multiply bases during exponent operations. For example, $2^3 \times 2^4 \neq 4^7$; it is $2^7$.

concepts.title: 2. Zero & Negative Exponents
concepts.subtitle: Understanding Non-Positive Exponents
concepts.summary: Any non-zero base raised to the power 0 equals 1. A negative exponent represents the reciprocal of the same base raised to the corresponding positive exponent.
concepts.trap: A negative exponent does NOT make the base number negative. For example, $3^{-2} = \frac{1}{9}$, not $-9$.

concepts.title: 3. Prime-Power Decomposition
concepts.subtitle: Breaking Down Composite Bases
concepts.summary: Express composite numbers as products of prime bases raised to exponents before applying exponent rules. This makes otherwise different-looking expressions comparable through common prime bases.

points.text: Identify Composite Bases: Identify bases that are not prime, such as $6, 12, 18, 72$ and $144$.
Factorize: Write each composite number as a product of prime factors. For example, $12 = 2^2 \times 3$.

concepts.trap: Do not combine powers whose bases are different. For example, $2^3 \times 3^2$ cannot be simplified to $6^5$.
